issue.title: Using warmstart in GradientBoostingClassifier produces inferior solution
issue.body:
<!--

For more information, see User Questions: http://scikit-learn.org/stable/support.html#user-questions
-->

<!-- Instructions For Filing a Bug: https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-bugs -->

#### Description
Using the warmstart flag for the `GradientBoostingClassifier` results in an inferior solution compared to fitting all base models at once. From how the docs regarding the warmstarting are written, I expect the results to be equal.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.ensemble
import sklearn.model_selection


X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_digits(return_X_y=True)
rs = np.random.RandomState(42)
indices = np.arange(X.shape[0])
rs.shuffle(indices)
indices = indices[:150]
X = X[indices]
y = y[indices]
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split(
    X, y, random_state=16,
)
classifier = sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingClassifier(
    warm_start=True, n_estimators=1, random_state=1,
)
classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
for i in range(99):
    classifier.n_estimators += 1
    classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(classifier.score(X_test, y_test))

classifier = sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingClassifier(
    n_estimators=100, random_state=1,
)
classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(classifier.score(X_test, y_test))
```

#### Expected Results
Two equal scores.

#### Actual Results
0.605263157895
0.657894736842

#### Versions
Linux-4.4.0-96-generic-x86_64-with-debian-stretch-sid
Python 3.6.2 |Continuum Analytics, Inc.| (default, Jul 20 2017, 13:51:32) 
[GCC 4.4.7 20120313 (Red Hat 4.4.7-1)]
NumPy 1.13.3
SciPy 0.19.1
Scikit-Learn 0.19.1

#### Edit

The following models have the same issue:
* ExtraTreesClassifier
* SGDClassifier
* PassiveAggressiveClassifier

The RandomForestClassifier seems to not have this problem and I did not test regression algorithms but expect them to behave the same.

body:
Two reasons for that:

- The learning rate is by default dynamic, it changes depending on the number of samples already seen. The counter is stored in `self.t_`. Calling `fit` a second time resets the counter, even with `warm_start=True`. ~~We might want to fix this.~~ Note that the counter does not restart when calling `partial_fit`.
To isolate this first issue, we can use `learning_rate='constant'`.

- The random state is not stored, as in `GradientBoostingClassifier` (see [here](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/102620f8d122d244dd08ccaa015d67a97d8a28ae/sklearn/ensemble/gradient_boosting.py#L1025-L1026)). Therefore, the random sample order is reset at each call of `fit` or `partial_fit`, even with `warm_start=True`. We might want to fix this.
To isolate this second issue, we can use `shuffle=False`.

I also rewrote your snippet, as you don't need to increase `self.max_iter` to add one more iteration, as in `GradientBoostingClassifier`. This API difference could be better documented.
You also need `tol=None` to avoid early stopping.

```py
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits
from sklearn.linear_model import SGDClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import warnings

# to ignore ConvergenceWarning
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

X, y = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
classes = np.unique(y)
n_iter = 10


def run(shuffle, learning_rate):
    for seed in range(10):
        X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
            X, y, random_state=seed)

        common_params = dict(learning_rate=learning_rate, eta0=0.01,
                             random_state=1, tol=None, shuffle=shuffle)
        clf_1 = SGDClassifier(max_iter=1, warm_start=True, **common_params)
        clf_2 = SGDClassifier(**common_params)
        clf_3 = SGDClassifier(max_iter=n_iter, **common_params)

        for i in range(n_iter):
            clf_1.fit(X_train, y_train)
            clf_2.partial_fit(X_train, y_train, classes=classes)
        clf_3.fit(X_train, y_train)

        score_1 = clf_1.score(X_test, y_test)
        score_2 = clf_2.score(X_test, y_test)
        score_3 = clf_3.score(X_test, y_test)

        print("\n", seed, score_1, score_2, score_3)


# issue 1: self.t_ is reset when calling fit with warm_start=True
run(shuffle=False, learning_rate='optimal')

print('\n\n')
# issue 2: random state is not stored
run(shuffle=True, learning_rate='constant')
```

Thank you for isolating these issues @TomDLT. Regarding the first issue, this should in my opinion either be changed or documented. It would be great if the second issue could be fixed am I'm happy to do this if this is wanted.

Regarding `max_iter` together with `warm_start`, the code is intended the way it is, meaning that I want to dynamically increase the number of maximally allowed iterations if the optimization did not converge, but maybe also stop earlier if I either run out of time or reach convergence. In case this could be achieved differently, I'm happy to learn about that.

issue.title: [MRG] Remove counter reset in SGD when warm_start=True
issue.body:
Fixes the first part of #10011

In SGD, the counter `self.t_` for dynamic learning rate was incorrectly reset when ``warm_start=True``

body:
~~I fixed the first issue in #10016.~~
EDIT: For the first issue, we need to have an equivalence between an implicit warm start (with `warm_start=True`), and an explicit one (giving the coefficients and intercept to the fit function).
If one really wants the counter not to be reset, `partial_fit` is the best solution.

___
The second is not easy to fix since the random state is "stored" inside the `SequentialDataset` object which accesses the data in SGD solver. The random state is contained in the shuffled sample order, which change after each iteration. Therefore, we don't have access to the random state of the shuffling, except by storing the entire permutation. I don't see an easy way to fix this issue, apart from rewriting the random behavior in the SGD solver.

That being said, I wonder what is your use case. Why do you want to use this outer for-loop?

Isn't the seed passed to the SGD function and then used when calling dataset.shuffle (https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/ac1b04875331fc291a437025a18ddfefd4051d7c/sklearn/linear_model/sgd_fast.pyx#L618)? Or do you mean that the current shuffling gets lost in a second call to `fit` because a new `SequentialDataset` object is created?

The reason I'm using SGD like this is when invoking the algorithm with a time limit during hyperparameter optimization. Plain SGD is quite fast, so that isn't an issue. However, if you do some heavy preprocessing it can take quite some time. As intermediate solutions might already be good enough, they can be used for the optimization procedure. 

Anyway, documenting the behavior is probably the easiest way to go. On average, the scores aren't really different, it is more like an unexpected behavior which looks like a bug at first sight.

> Or do you mean that the current shuffling gets lost in a second call to fit because a new SequentialDataset object is created?

Exactly

> On average, the scores aren't really different

Indeed, after all it is a stochastic algorithm.

> Anyway, documenting the behavior is probably the easiest way to go

I agree.
I think @mfeurer's expectation is ok for ``partial_fit``, but not for ``warm_start``.

Was there a reason for using ``warm_start`` instead of ``partial_fit``? Though I guess the use-case is more semantically similar to ``warm_start``, and for the tree-based methods we have that warmstarts yield the same models... hm...

The reason why I used `warm_start` is because worked well for tree-based models, so I thought I just refactor all models in auto-sklearn to work in a similar way. Having figured this out, I will go back to using `partial_fit`, but use it without `warm_start`. As @TomDLT already mentioned the docs need to be updated. Shall I go ahead and add some lines to the `SGDClassifier`, `SGDRegressor` and probably also the passive aggressive family?

> Shall I go ahead and add some lines to the SGDClassifier, SGDRegressor and probably also the passive aggressive family?

please do :)

It's a bit weird that the behavior is different between trees and linear models, though ... but I guess the use-cases are different, too. Working on hyperband these days? ;) did you see https://github.com/zygmuntz/hyperband ?

issue.title: DOC add docs about sgd and warmstarting (#10011)
issue.body:
In particular, clarify for SGDClassifier, SGDRegressor, PassiveAggressiveClassifier and PassiveAggressiveRegressor how the attribute warm_start and the methods `fit` and `partial_fit`
interact.

This is a first draft on documenting this behavior and I'm happy to get feedback of whether the underlying issue gets clearer.

Fixes #10011

body:
I added a first draft in #10087.

@amueller nope, that's just an undocumented feature of Auto-sklearn that I needed to adapt because of the change in scikit-learn.
